Dear Secretary Reese:

        Pursuant to Section 205 of the Federal Power Act (“FPA”), 16 U.S.C. § 824d, and Part 35
of the regulations of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (“FERC” or “Commission”),
                                                               1
Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc. (“MISO”), on behalf of the Hoosier Energy
Rural Electric Cooperative, Inc. (“Hoosier”), respectfully submits for filing its proposed modified
Attachment O to the MISO Open Access Transmission, Energy and Operating Reserve Markets
Tariff (“Tariff”) and requests certain modifications to its company-specific formula rate template
(“Formula Rate”) and protocols (“Protocols”) to transition Hoosier from an Annual Transmission
Revenue Requirement (“ATRR”) calculated on a historic basis to one that is forward-looking and
                                                  2
to ensure compliance with FERC Order No. 898.

        As discussed below, Hoosier respectfully requests certain changes to the MISO Tariff to
allow it to recover its ATRR through a forward-looking Formula Rate proposed and supported
herein. Hoosier respectfully requests an effective date of January 1, 2027.

       and reserves the right to comment or protest.

       (2023) (“Order No. 898”).

I.     BACKGROUND

       A. Description of MISO

        MISO is a Commission-approved RTO providing open access transmission service and
administering day-ahead, real-time, and financial transmission rights markets in a region
consisting of fifteen states and one Canadian province. MISO ensures reliable operation of, and
open access to, high-voltage power lines across its footprint. MISO was approved as the nation’s
                    3
first RTO in 2001.

       B. Description of the Hoosier Energy Rural Electric Cooperative, Inc.

        Hoosier is a member-owned generation and transmission cooperative organized under the
laws of the state of Indiana. Hoosier’s purpose is to provide generation and transmission service
to its seventeen cooperative members in Indiana and Illinois. Hoosier is a transmission-owning
member of MISO, and owns and operates generation and transmission facilities in the MISO
region.

II.    DESCRIPTION OF FILING

        Hoosier requests certain changes to the MISO Tariff to allow it to recover its ATRR
through a forward-looking Formula Rate. The proposed Formula Rate -includes modifications to
the existing company-specific Attachment O of the MISO Tariff (“Attachment O-HE”) and
company-specific Protocols that govern the projected net revenue requirement. Specifically,
Hoosier proposes a forward-looking transmission formula rate for recovering transmission costs
under Attachment O-HE based on its projected net revenue requirement to be trued-up to Hoosier’s
actual net revenue requirement. The proposed formula rate changes how the formula inputs are
developed and do not modify the formula rate itself. Hoosier’s actual net revenue requirement will
                                                                                    4
be based on its RUS Form 12 template in accordance with the proposed Protocols. Additionally,
Hoosier proposes modified Protocols similar to those used by other transmission owners that use
a forward-looking Attachment O formula rate. They are modeled after the existing Protocols and
edited to include the calculation of an Annual True-Up, True-Up Adjustment, and second open
                     5
stakeholder meeting.

       Hoosier is not subject to the Commission’s ratemaking jurisdiction under Sections 205 and
                                                  6
206 of the FPA because it is not a public utility. However, under Sections 205 and 206 of the
FPA, the Commission does have jurisdiction over the rates for transmission service provided by

MISO. In this regard, the courts have made clear that when a non-jurisdictional transmission
owner voluntarily joins an RTO, the Commission “can ensure by examining [the non-jurisdictional

utility’s revenue requirement] that the [RTO’s] rates will ultimately be just and reasonable.”

        Redlined and clean tariff sheets showing the proposed Attachment O-HE are provided as
Exhibits attached to this filing. Additionally, witness Nate Knopf, Hoosier’s Senior Transmission
Economic and Policy Analyst, has provided testimony regarding various aspects of this filing as
Exhibit No. HE-001. Finally, a populated projected Formula Rate with associated workpapers is
also provided as an Exhibit.

       A. Revisions to Attachment O to Effectuate Forward-Looking Rate

        Hoosier is proposing certain modifications to its company-specific Formula Rate to
calculate its ATRR on a forward-looking basis. Hoosier’s company-specific Formula Rate is a
modified version of MISO Generic Attachment O RUS Form 12 non-levelized rate template,
which is a historic formula rate template. As further described in the testimony of Mr. Knopf,
Hoosier has made certain changes to the MISO Attachment O – RUS Form 12 non-levelized rate
                                                    9
template to accommodate forward-looking recovery. Specifically, Hoosier is proposing to recover
its transmission costs on a forward-looking basis to align the timing of its investments with the
timing of recovery from rate payers.

       As the Commission has explained, “a forward-looking formula rate, if properly designed
                                                                      10
and supported, is a reasonable means to avoid lag in cost recovery.” Moreover, using forward-
looking estimated costs is not a departure from ratemaking practice, and, even if rates may initially
increase under a forward-looking approach, “customers will ultimately only pay the cost of service
                                              11
they would have paid on the lagging basis.”

        Currently, Hoosier is the only Indiana MISO Utility operating on a historical filed rate.
However, a forward-looking filed rate creates better financial alignment for a transmission owner
that is expanding its transmission asset base. In its past two five-year plans, Hoosier has seen a
25% increase in proposed transmission spending, and transmission spending is expected to
continue to increase substantially. Hoosier estimates $200,000,000 of grants for Grid Resilience
and Innovation Partnerships transmission projects. Under the proposed Formula Rate, transmission

strengthen borrowing power and the financial agility needed to deliver affordable, reliable power
through increasing industry turmoil.

             (i)    Use of Estimates and True-Up in Attachment O-HE

        The proposed true-up mechanism ensures that MISO ratepayers pay the actual revenue
requirement for Hoosier’s transmission costs by trueing up the estimated revenue requirement to
audited actual financial documents and RUS Form 12 schedules and ensuring repayment with
interest for over or under collection. The change to a forward-looking test year will affect the
timing of revenue recovery, but customers will pay the same cost of service across the life of the
transmission projects that they would have absent this change. The Commission has accepted
nearly similar modifications, while accounting for some unique differences, to the Attachment O
                                                12
template for other MISO Transmission Owners.

        As further described in the Testimony of Mr. Knopf, Hoosier will populate the RUS Form
12 schedules in Attachment O. 13 The total True-Up Adjustment will be calculated after Hoosier
completes its RUS Form 12 schedules for the prior year. The True-Up Adjustment represents the
sum of the excess or shortfall due to the actual versus projected revenue requirement and the excess
or shortfall due to volume differences the actual versus projected volume.

            (ii)    Description of Formula Rate Protocols

        Hoosier proposes modifications to its company-specific Protocols. The proposed Protocols
are similar to those employed by other transmission owners that use a forward-looking Attachment
O formula rate. They are modeled after existing protocols and edited to include the calculation of
an Annual True-Up, True-Up Adjustment, and second open stakeholder meeting. 14 Consistent with
the Commission’s instructions to other MISO entities with forward-looking formula rates, the
proposed Protocols satisfy the Commission’s concerns with respect to (i) scope of participation
(i.e., who can participate in the information exchange); (ii) the transparency of the information
exchange (i.e., what information is exchanged); and (iii) the ability of customers to challenge
transmission owners’ implementation of the formula rate as a result of the information exchange

           (iii)   Modifications to Attachment O for Order No. 898 Compliance

        Although Hoosier does not currently own any energy storage facilities, Hoosier proposes
certain modifications to its company-specific Attachment O-HE template to ensure compliance
with Order No. 898, the Commission’s Final Rule amending the Uniform System of Accounts to
create new accounts for wind, solar, and other renewable generating assets, create a new functional
class for energy storage accounts, and create new accounts within existing functions for computer
hardware, software, and communications equipment. The modifications add lines for the inclusion
of energy storage plant balances and expenses, as well as lines to calculate an allocation factor for
the inclusion of energy storage plant in ISO rates similar to the TP allocation factor already
calculated in the template. The proposed modifications are outlined in Exhibit No. HE-005 and are
                                                                                                   20
consistent with those accepted for MISO transmission owners in FERC Docket No. ER 25-323.

           (iv)    Attachment GG and Attachment MM

         As discussed in the Testimony of Mr. Knopf, Hoosier also proposes a company-specific
Attachment GG true-up procedure. The annual revenue requirement for MISO-designated projects
accepted under Attachment FF is not included in the Attachment O net revenue requirement and
is instead calculated pursuant to a formula set forth in Attachment GG or Attachment MM. Hoosier
proposes to use the pro forma Attachment GG and Attachment MM formula rate templates as
provided in the MISO Tariff with no changes. The pro forma Attachment GG template is already
set up to use a forward-looking revenue requirement with a subsequent true-up. However, while
the pro forma Attachment GG template includes a column for a FERC-accepted True-Up
Adjustment, there are no generic true-up procedures. Therefore, Hoosier proposes a company-
specific Attachment GG true-up procedures consistent with the procedures accepted by the
                                                       21
Commission for Dairyland Power Cooperative. The proposed Attachment GG True-Up
Procedures are in Exhibit No. HE-008. Hoosier will use the pro form Attachment MM template
and intends to calculate true up adjustments using the pro forma Attachment MM True Up
Adjustment – Aggregate template.

       B. Hoosier’s 2027 Forward-Looking Revenue Requirement

       Hoosier requests that the implementation of the forward-looking calculation be effective
January 1, 2027. Exhibit No. HE-002 is the 2027 Attachment O-HE Populated Formula Rate. The
2027 projected revenue requirement was developed using the proposed Attachment O-HE and
Hoosier’s most recent forecast for cost-of-service components for the year ending December 31,
2027. The inputs to the revenue requirement are 13-month average plant in service and
accumulated depreciation reserves balances for December 31, 2026, through December 31, 2027,
along with 13-month average balances for plant held for future use, prepayments, materials and
